reference: GNU coreutils chgrp for private file metadata with the GID already owned by the fixture; no users, authentication, capabilities or group memberships change. Bash help/type are metadata contracts.
coverage: Numeric existing-group application, symlink default/-h, multiple paths with a missing middle file, missing operands and unknown group.
Bash registration and documented help metadata only for the metadata cases.
exclusions: Changing to distinct GIDs and controlled named-group resolution remain deferred for a disposable VM or syscall mock.

cases.purpose: Confirm through Bash's documented type -t interface that the statically compiled chgrp name is registered as a builtin, without invoking it.
Check the synopsis registered for chgrp using Bash's help -s builtin interface; this checks metadata only.
Check Bash's long help text against the documented chgrp description and usage line, without running an ownership operation.
cases.stdout:
chgrp: chgrp GROUP FILE...
    Change file group.
    
    chgrp [-h] GROUP FILE...   GROUP is a name or numeric id.

cases.purpose: Compare a valid named group, an unknown group name, and a numeric group ID against GNU using a controlled group database; verify status and resulting metadata for successful calls.
cases.reason: Numeric and unknown-name obligations executed and passed; named resolution through chgrp itself never ran, and distinct-gid resolution needs driver-provisioned identities.

cases.purpose: Apply the existing fixture GID to two private files and verify contents and mode preservation.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
printf second > other
chmod 640 data
chgrp "$gid" data other
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; a=os.stat("data"); b=os.stat("other"); assert a.st_gid == b.st_gid; print(oct(a.st_mode & 0o777), open("data").read())'

cases.purpose: Exercise default and -h symlink policy using the already-owned GID, preserving the private link and target.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
ln -s data link
chgrp "$gid" link
chgrp -h "$gid" link
[[ -L link ]]

cases.purpose: A missing middle file reports failure while valid neighbors use an already-owned fixture GID.
cases.script:
printf private > data
gid=$(/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; print(os.stat("data").st_gid)')
printf tail > after
chgrp "$gid" data missing after

cases.purpose: Compare a missing-operand error rejected before any file ownership syscall.
An unknown group is rejected without changing the private file.
cases.script:
printf private > data
chgrp fixture-group-that-does-not-exist data
